382	### Spikes
383	
384	Each rule is fixed here, before its run. A spike runs in CJ0 or at the head of the phase that
385	needs it, and its verdict is recorded as the decision named. Paid runs are behind `--live --cap`,
386	held to P-6's ledger and the month's budget, and read the key only through
387	`tools/proof/assistant_prompt_eval.py`'s `anthropic_key()`.
388	
389	- **FC-S1 — Sound Analysis as a signal (before FC3; verdict FC-30).** Question: on macOS 26.5.1,
390	  does `.version1` find laughter, applause and cheering in the owner's recordings well enough to
391	  steer the pool, how fast, and at which window? Inputs: the events sample (S-EV, with the
392	  owner's written onset list), 10 minutes of speech only (S-TH), a talk over music (S-MU), and
393	  `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`. Runs: windows 1.0, 1.5 and 3.0 s at overlap 0.5, through
394	  `SNAudioFileAnalyzer` and through `SNAudioStreamAnalyzer` fed by `speechReader`. **Rule:**
395	  - A group is first-class when one threshold t ∈ {0.3, 0.4, …, 0.8}, chosen on the
396	    odd-numbered labelled events and applied unchanged to the even-numbered ones, finds at least
397	    70 % of them (an onset within ±1 s) and calls at most one window per 10 minutes of S-TH and
398	    S-MU that group. A group that fails is weak.
399	  - The window kept is the one with the best laughter recall among those whose run is at least
400	    60× real time. A tie goes to 1.5 s. If no window reaches 60×, the pass covers only the
401	    scope's played spans.
402	  - The stream analyzer is used if its event times agree with the file analyzer's within one
403	    hop. Otherwise the cache records which one ran and FC-31 is amended.
404	- **FC-S2 — The ranking's request shape and cost (before FC5's code; verdicts FC-50's constants,
405	  FC-51, FC-63).** Question: does the helper as it is, configured with one app tool
406	  `submit_ranking` and no deferred tool, send a request the API accepts? Does `countTokens`
407	  count the same body? Does `claude-opus-5-5` submit a valid ranking on its first call? What
408	  does a run cost against the estimate? Inputs: the owner's episode transcript (S-EP) if it
409	  exists, else S-TH's, and two public-domain texts cut into timed sentences at 2.6 words per
410	  second (their sources named in the spike's README). Runs: 10 in all at counts 10, 20 and 30,
411	  cap $3.00. **Rule:**
412	  - (a) and (b) pass if no request is refused. If the request without a deferred tool is refused,
413	    FC5's diff adds `search: false` to `configure` (FC-51).
414	  - (c) passes if at least 9 of 10 runs submit a valid ranking (FC-63's checks) on the first call
415	    and 10 of 10 within two. If it fails, FC5's diff instead adds a one-shot `rank` message using
416	    structured output (`output_config.format`), and FC6 is designed on that.
417	  - (d) passes if every run's priced cost lies within [`low`, `ceiling`] computed before it. The
418	    10th and 90th percentiles of output tokens per candidate become FC-50's constants.
419	- **FC-S3 — Sentence ends and transcript size (before FC4; verdict FC-41's gap, FC-62's numbers).**
420	  Question: do this Mac's words end sentences often enough to cut at sentence ends, and how many
421	  tokens does a transcript cost? Inputs: S-TH or S-EP, transcribed on-device and once by
422	  AssemblyAI (one request, at most $0.50, with `disfluencies` and speakers; it also becomes
423	  FC8a's filler fixture). **Rule:**
424	  - On-device sentence ends are usable if at least 80 % of AssemblyAI's sentence ends have an
425	    on-device sentence end (FC-41) within 0.5 s, and the two sentence counts are within 30 % of
426	    each other.
427	  - Otherwise FC-41's on-device rule becomes "a word ending `.?!…` or a gap of 0.6 s", and the
428	    Find Clips window says that edges are approximate without a cloud transcript.
429	  - Tokens per word, from `countTokens` (free) on both transcripts, are recorded for FC-62.

930	- Louder lines by volume, for loudness peaks.
931	- `assemblyai_fake.py` transcripts with punctuation, speakers, disfluencies, and both values of
932	  `remote_deleted`.
933	- `anthropic_fake.py` with scripted submissions and a `count_tokens` route.
934	- Public-domain texts as timed transcripts (FC-S2).
935	
936	Sound events cannot be synthesised credibly. Without S-EV, FC3 proves only timing and stamps,
937	using the `speech` group's onset, and FC-30 waits for the sample.
938	
939	### Risks
940	
941	- **Ranking quality is the whole product.** A ranked list a creator does not trust is worse than
942	  none. FC9's trial is the test, and prompt changes after it cost paid runs under the month's
943	  budget.
944	- **Sound Analysis may be weak on real podcasts.** Soft chuckles are hard to hear, music beds and
945	  game audio confuse it, and the pre-spike reading already called speech `music` at 1 s windows.
946	  FC-30 can demote a group to weak, and then only the words carry the ranking.
947	- **Sentence edges on-device.** If FC-S3 fails, edges are approximate without a cloud transcript.
948	- **Time on first run.** Recognising a two-hour episode on-device takes minutes. After that, TR-14's
949	  cache and FC-32's cache make it instant.
950	- **Cost and length.** An eight-hour VOD's transcript can pass FC-62's cap, and a model the price
951	  table lacks cannot be priced in advance. Both are refused or said, never guessed.
952	- **Text leaves the Mac.** The transcript goes to Anthropic at Rank. FC-64 says so before the
953	  press, and a creator with a guest's recording may still need the guest's consent; the guide
954	  says so.
955	- **Classifier refusals.** A transcript about security or medicine can trip a safety classifier.
956	  `fallbacks: "default"` retries on another model at its own price, and the cost line shows what
957	  was billed.
958	- **The helper is shared with Rasterize.** FC5's diff must land in both, or `agent/src` stops
959	  being one file set. It is one issue, filed at FC5.
960	- **Range edges.** Transitions, ramps, timed caption pages, nests and linked pairs at an edge are
961	  where `keep_range` can go wrong. FC1's tests cover each kind, and FC2 proves frames and samples
962	  against the source.
963	- **Many documents.** Thirty shorts opened at once would approach the instance's
964	  forty-document deadlock; FC-82 closes each after queueing.
965	- **Bet 3's interface.** FC9 needs bet 3's planner as a function applied to a document it did
966	  not create. If bet 3 lands only as a command that makes its own copy, FC9 makes two documents
967	  per short until that is fixed.
968	- **Consolidated media.** A source whose media sits inside its own package gives shorts that
969	  point into that package; moving it means a relink. Media files are never copied (FC-21).
970	
971	### Not in this bet
972	
973	- Any score, virality figure or engagement prediction (FC-67).
974	- Ranking without an Anthropic key, on-device ranking, or Apple FoundationModels.
975	- Ranking for an outside agent inside Frame Job (`find_clips` answers the analysis; the agent
976	  ranks).
977	- Publishing, scheduling, platform upload, titles or thumbnails for platforms.
978	- Finding clips across several projects or a footage library, or a `search_media` index.
979	- B-roll, music, zooms or punch-ins added to a short. Punch in on cuts is the next tier.
980	- Removing pauses in a short. It is a later option, asked at FC8a.
981	- Linked vertical versions that follow the source's later edits. That is bet 3's to decide.
982	- Translated captions, platform safe-zone overlays and named platform export rows (the next
983	  tier's publish slice).
984	- Visual signals (faces, gestures, shot changes) as readings. Bet 3's and bet 6's Vision
985	  analysis may add them later.
986

content.content:
## The bets

The bets are ranked by how many creators each reaches, how often they would use it, and how far it puts Frame Job ahead rather than level, discounted by effort and risk.

Every bet has the same shape. Analysis that Frame Job already caches, or that macOS provides on the device, feeds a planner. The planner writes edits the core already knows how to make. Each result is therefore an ordinary undo step on a real timeline, and each command becomes an MCP tool that the Assistant and outside agents can run with no new agent work.

Effort is build effort (S, M, L, XL), never lines of code.

| Rank | Bet | Effort | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transcript tab | L | Everyone who records themselves talking |
| 2 | Screen recordings with the cursor as data | L | Screencasts, tutorials, courses, product demos |
| 3 | Make Vertical Version | M (copy), L (linked versions) | Everyone who posts shorts |
| 4 | Find Clips | M on top of 3 | Podcasters, long-form YouTubers, streamers |
| 5 | Switch by Speaker, and every audio track | M | Video podcasts and interviews |
| 6 | Camera cutout and layouts | L | Screencasters, talking heads, streamers |

Bets 1 and 2 remove the two points where talking creators and the home segment give up. Bets 3 and 4 complete the long-to-short loop. Bet 5 takes the podcast format on the strength of the audio chain. Bet 6 closes the presenter-camera gap.

### 1. Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review
### 3. Make Vertical Version

**Pitch.** File ▸ Make Vertical Version… writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes. OpusClip [C11], CapCut [C4], Premiere [P21], Final Cut Pro for iPad [P17], Riverside [C9], Kapwing [C20] and Screen Studio [S1] all ship it, and auto-repurposing is the most-wanted creator AI feature in one survey [D2]. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026 [C4]. Here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with a framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.

**Builds on.** `fill_scale` (`edit_fit.rs`); Add Blurred Background (`edit_background.rs`); word captions sized to the shorter side (`CaptionStyle.swift`); graphics that read `ctx.canvas`; actions (`edit_action.rs`); nests (`edit_nest.rs`); `set_canvas` (`edit_canvas.rs`); File ▸ Duplicate; the E9 Vision spike in `tools/proof/effects_spike/`.

**Effort.** M as a regenerated copy. L for linked versions, which need a canvas per version, framing overrides per clip and a format bump.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it first. The reason given there, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies: the analysis runs offline and its output is actions.
- No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already carries an action (a zoom, a grade, a ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at.
- `set_canvas` does not rescale action end states. A screencast's existing zoom actions keep their 16:9 targets, and the planner must rewrite them.
- `MediaCacheLane` is a width-2 lane for audio decodes, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows.
- The planner should use face, human and saliency rectangles with tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found that foreground masks flicker on video.
- Two people in frame, a speaker leaving the frame, and shot changes inside one flattened clip each need a rule.

### 4. Find Clips

**Pitch.** Clip ▸ Find Clips…, run on an episode, a VOD or a finished edit, lists 10 to 30 candidates of 20 to 60 seconds. Each candidate shows:

- in and out points snapped to sentence ends;
- its length;
- a one-line reason, such as "laughter after the punchline";
- a preview.

There is no virality score. Make Short turns the checked candidates into vertical projects through bet 3. Each short is word-captioned, has fillers removed where a cloud transcript exists, and is queued for export.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Long-to-short is what OpusClip [C10] [C12], Riverside [C9], Submagic [C14] and Kapwing [C20] sell, all metered by credits. YouTube's own free tool covers only 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Frame Job pulls ahead in three ways:

- **Local signals.** Laughter, applause and cheering from Sound Analysis, the 10 ms loudness, speech spans and sentence ends are all measured on the Mac.
- **The creator's own key.** Ranking runs on the creator's Claude key, with no per-minute credits.
- **Real timelines.** Each candidate opens as an editable timeline.

A stated reason for each moment, rather than a score, answers the documented complaint that clippers cut in the wrong place [D16].

**Builds on.** `get_transcript` (timeline ticks); `ClipLoudness.swift` and the per-media loudness cache; `media_speech.rs`; `detect_fillers` and `ripple_delete_ranges`; caption Restyle with Replace; the Export Queue; the Assistant helper (`agent/`) and its price table; `set_range`.

**Effort.** M on top of bet 3. Without bet 3 it produces horizontal clips only.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Ranking quality is the whole product.
- On-device FoundationModels has a 4,096-token context and needs Apple Intelligence turned on. It is a chunked, weaker fallback, not an equal path.
- Speaker labels exist only on AssemblyAI transcripts requested with speakers.
- No op copies a timeline range into a new project: `new_project` takes a path, and Duplicate copies everything. One is needed.
- Sound Analysis (`SNClassifySoundRequest` `.version1`, 303 labels on macOS 26.5.1, laughter, applause and cheering among them) is noisy on game audio and music beds.
- Long transcripts cost tokens, so show an estimate range before running.

### 5. Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file
## Decisions for the owner

1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
   - A plugin system: stays out.
3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
   - AI-10, for Proposals.
   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].

## Sources

content.content:
# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`

  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is

  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.

  here, D2-1). Checked ONCE on decode, read by BINARY SEARCH both ways
  (`source(atClip:)`, `clip(atSource:)`), because a ramp holds a point every
  600 ticks and the waveform and the silence walk read per column and per
  bucket; `SourceMaps` is how a reader is handed the maps of its snapshot's
  handle. A reader takes the map only when it is `ramped`, so a constant
  clip keeps today's arithmetic exactly. `rate` is the core's rate profile
  (`RatePoint`s, SR-26), checked on decode; a list that fails the check is
  [] and the map is kept. `TimelineView+SourceMap.swift` is
  the filmstrip's and the waveform's map-aware `sourceTime`
  (`TimelineView.swift` is frozen; it holds only `sourceMaps`, set in
  `refreshTimeline` from the same handle as the snapshot).
- `DuckSpeech.swift` — Duck by Speech's Swift half (spec §11 AU-110, AU-111,
  AU-113): `spans` (VAD probabilities → source-tick spans: p ≥
  `defaultVoiceConfidence`, gaps under 0.2 s bridged, ends clamped to the
  media's duration), `ops` (the `set_media_speech` each media without spans
  needs, or a `Refusal` naming the clip or the file), `problem` (the same
  answer without reading a cache, for the popup), and `DuckCurves` (one
  handle's plan `ducks`, decoded lazily once, for the timeline). Every duck
  edit of a Speech duck, in the Ducking section and over `set_audio`, puts
  `ops` before the `set_audio`. No span→time or gain arithmetic: that is
  the core's.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- Pitfalls, each measured: **a section factory is not a section until
  `makeSections()` calls it** — nothing type-checks the omission, and two
  phases shipped a section invisible in the app; `editedList` — a write of a
  list-valued key is built from the list it is about to REPLACE (the action's
  end list, else the base), never the evaluated one; the collapsed-state
  `UserDefaults` key records COLLAPSED, so `defaultExpanded` applies only when
  nothing is stored; a field's `refresh` is skipped while its field editor is
  attached, which it still is inside `controlTextDidEndEditing`; the pane's
  low-priority bottom pin is **249**, one below `.defaultLow`, because at 250
  it tied with a section's hugging and the solver picked per PROCESS; and
  `rebuild()` destroys every control and preserves no first responder, so a
  control a person TYPES into must live outside `structureSignature` and be
  applied to views that already exist (`MediaPane.arrange()` is the shape).

  · `AssistantComposer.swift` · `AssistantTranscript.swift` · `AssistantContextMeter.swift` — the
  Assistant tab (road map 12 A2, spec §11 AI-4). The pane builds its ONE
  `AssistantView` in `init`, never in `makeSections()` (a rebuild would take
  the composer's first responder), calls `onAssistantView` with it, and is
  exactly the visible height (`== 0` at priority 1 under the controller's
  `>=`), so the transcript scrolls itself. **The views hold no
  conversation**: the transcript is `EditorViewController.assistantTranscript`
  (`AssistantTranscript`, Rasterize's `handleEvent` ported as storage — a
  delta extends the last entry only while the previous event was the same
  delta type; `argumentSummary` drops `project`; road map 13 P2: it sums the
  `cost` events from `turn_started` to `turn_finished` into an
  `AssistantTurnCost` and ends the turn with its line as `.meta`, and
  `clear()` and `endConversation` reset the sum; road map 13 P4: every `cost`
  also adds to `conversationCost` and emits `.conversationCost`, and `clear()`
  and `endConversation` reset it and emit `.conversationCost` BEFORE their
  `.usage`, which `assistant_tab_probe`'s P1 needs last), the question the session's
  `pendingQuestion`, the session `EditorViewController.assistant`; a floating
  window later calls `attachAssistant` with the same view. **Return never
  answers**: Allow and Deny are `OptionButtonControl`s (a click, no key), Send
  is a 64 pt `AccentButton` with no key equivalent that reads Stop while busy
  or asking, and the composer's bare Return sends only while idle and beeps
  otherwise; a modified Return is a new line (spec §11 AI-17, K-2). No spinner
  (the harness settles). A label's frame is 2 pt wider
  than its text each side, and a row that holds a wrapping label is inset by 2
  pt; `snapshot_ui`'s outside_superview rule measures alignment rects since
  #140 and no longer needs the inset, which is kept. `AssistantTranscriptView`
  is a scroll view owning ONE non-editable, selectable TextKit 1 text view
  (spec §11 AI-17): each entry is a UTF-16 range of its one text (`spans`),
  one "\n" between entries, so a selection and a plain-text copy cross entries
  — its writable type is the legacy `NSStringPboardType`, because
  `writeSelection` answers false for `.string` (measured, B18); `.extended`

  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one

  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —

  bits, never dithered. Where the sound ends is `ExportAudioEnd`'s
  (spec §11 #337): exactly round(range × 48 000) frames, the crossing buffer
  cut, later buffers read and dropped, a short read padded with silence at
  the master's depth; the measurement feeds the same count. The alpha movie rows' frames (`prores_4444`,
  `hevc_alpha`) are straightened in the video pump before `retimed`:
  un-premultiplied, each transparent pixel within 4 px of a visible one
  filled with the nearest one's colour, and labelled `StraightAlpha`, with
  `hevc_alpha`'s encoder key straight too (`ExportStraightAlpha.swift`, spec
  §11 G-35): `prores_4444`'s in place in float, `hevc_alpha`'s rounded first
  into a pooled 32BGRA buffer (`ExportFrames`, `ExportStraightAlphaHalf.swift`,
  PR-3); the fill is one generic pass over `StraightAlphaLayout` (`BGRA8`,
  `RGBAHalf`), whose `allVisible` keeps the whole-row check vectorised.
  `h264`'s and `hevc`'s frames are rounded to 8 bits the same way and not
  straightened, and `hevc` is pinned to Main; `hevc_10bit` maps to `.hevc`
  too, is told apart by its codec name (`isMain10`), is pinned to Main 10
  and, like every other row, gets the frame as drawn.
  `ExportWriter` FILLS the frame when a fit would leave at most
  a pixel uncovered, or — the frame a canvas-SHAPED size less at most one
  pixel on each axis, `(bw + a)·ch == (bh + b)·cw` for some `a`, `b` in
  {0, 1}, at any scale — when a fill would overshoot by at most one
  (`shapeGap`: `gap <= limit`, in integers), and letterboxes past that, where
  an alpha-carrying movie row (`prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`) is refused instead
  (padding inverts the alpha; a pure scale is fine); so no size of the
  canvas's own shape is refused for being odd, and a typed size of another
  shape is judged as the even frame it becomes; the frame is the size the
  CORE resolved, already even where the row needs it (spec §11 G-33), and
  `encodedSize` is only the floor under it; a missing encoder is
  `.presetUnavailable` and no file (`Exporter.encoderOutcome`, in
  `ExporterErrors.swift`, applied where `startWriting` hears the pipeline); `apng` FITS instead and must not
  grow the guard. GIF and APNG refuse past 600 frames rather than truncate.
  `renderFrame` is documented off-main. Audio export is NOT bit-deterministic
  within an 8 ms window at a duck ramp edge (AVFoundation's mix); a duck-free
  project decodes byte-identical. `ExportError` is `ExporterErrors.swift`'s.
  An export PINS the `GraphicSet` it was handed for its whole life, GATES it
  before the build (`ExporterGraphics.graphicsRefusal`: a graphic clip in
  the range, or in any nest reached from one, however deep, whose module did
  not compile or is missing, refuses before the destination is touched), and
  ABORTS on a recorded failure: `pollProgress` cancels and `finish` removes
  the file and answers `.graphicFailed`, whatever the pipeline said.
  `startWriting` starts the graphic prefetch (`startGraphicPrefetch`, G-26)
  after the pipeline is picked, and `releaseRecipeKey` (from `finish` and
  `deinit`) `stop`s it on the line before the `unpin`, then releases the
  export's ramp-audio wants — dispatched off the caller's thread from
  `deinit`, which can run inside `RampAudioRenders.wait`'s lock.
  `Exporter.graphicWarnings` (`ExporterGraphics.swift`'s
  `ExportGraphicWarning`, each (name, message) once with its first frame) is

  (G-24 (c)).

content.content:
# Spec §11 — decisions: The Assistant (road map 12)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed; its condensed record is `designs/adr/roadmap-12-assistant.md`
(the original is `archive/roadmap-12.md`, whose §4 made them, amended by the user's answers
in §6).

- **AI-1 — The assistant is a bundled helper, and the app never calls Anthropic itself.**
  `Contents/Helpers/framejob-agent` is Bun-compiled from `agent/` on the Anthropic TypeScript
  SDK's Tool Runner, as Rasterize builds its own (road map 12 §1, §2). It is the one TypeScript
  in the product; G-11 ("no TypeScript") governs graphic Modules and is untouched. The Swift
  side uses `Process`, pipes and GCD, so W-8's `async` confinement holds. Risk accepted: Bun in
  every `make app`, and a nested executable of H1's size, signed separately.
  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): `Contents/Helpers/reelcut-agent` is now
  `Contents/Helpers/framejob-agent`.
- **AI-2 — The helper owns no tools; every call goes through `AgentServer.execute` by way of
  one lane.** An `AgentLane` holds one lock around every tool call from either caller, the MCP
  trampoline and the assistant session; the trampoline's call to it is the only wiring change
  in the frozen `AgentServer.swift`. The lane routes a call to main, or leaves it on its own
  queue for the `offMainTools` (§3a), and the session never takes the lock on main, because an
  off-main tool holding it waits for main (§3b). The same gate, parity check, refusals and undo
  steps apply; there are no assistant-only tools. Risk accepted: one lock serializes both
  callers, so a long off-main call (`export`, up to 3600 s) holds the other.
- **AI-3 — The catalog and the gate are prepared at launch, not at `start()`.**
  `prepareCatalog()` builds the catalog, runs `noteArguments` and runs the parity check;
  `start()` and the assistant both call it, because the gate treats a tool it has no schema for
  as taking nothing (§3c). A `make test`-reachable probe proves that an assistant call with an
  argument succeeds in a launch WITHOUT `-AgentServerEnabled`. Risk accepted: the catalog is
  built and parity-checked at every launch, whether used or not.
- **AI-4 — The Assistant is the inspector's fourth tab: Clip, Media, Document, Assistant.** This
  amends the sharp handoff's "no assistant panel" line, which was about Rasterize's parts
  rather than this feature (§3e); it gets a menu item with a key (spec §9). The user chose the
  tab to start and may move it to a floating window after trying it (§6.1), so the pane holds
  only views: the session, the transcript's storage and the pending confirmation live outside
  it, and a move is a new host for the same views. One conversation per window; the session
  lives on `EditorViewController` and survives tab switches, pane rebuilds and inspector
  collapse (§3h). Risk accepted: the transcript gets only the inspector's width, and showing it
  hides the other tabs.
- **AI-5 — The assistant edits its own window's project.** The lane pins the call's document
  the way `callScope` pins the scope: a per-call `callDocument` that `targetDocument` checks
  first, cleared by a `defer`. A `project` argument naming a DIFFERENT open project is refused
  by name, because an untitled project has no path and a window switch mid-turn would move the
  next edit (§3d). Risk accepted: one conversation cannot edit a second open project.
- **AI-6 — W-9 governs automatic styling, not a person's request.** No PIPELINE picks words by
  meaning. The assistant writes a caption's text or style only because the person asked it to
  in the conversation, and each such edit is an ordinary undo step (§3g). Risk accepted: a
  person may ask for emphasis by meaning, which no pipeline may do.
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-5:** the same holds for cutting words. When the person asks,
  the assistant may choose words to cut by their meaning (a false start), reading them through
  `get_transcript`, a clip's words in timeline times that never makes a network call. It
  proposes, then makes ordinary undoable cuts; no pipeline picks words to cut by meaning.
- **AI-7 — What the assistant may not call, and what it must ask about first.** Withheld: the
  dev tools, always (V-1: they are not in Distribution, and the assistant sees one catalog in
  both builds); `record_screen`, always, because recording is a person at the Record button;
  and `transcribe` with the cloud engine, refused with R6-2's sentence and pointing at File ▸
  Generate Captions…. Ask first: `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project` and
  `consolidate_media`, because each writes files where the model chose (§3f, §6.3). Such a call
  is NOT run when the helper asks; the transcript shows a confirmation row naming the tool and
  where it writes, with Allow and Deny, and the helper's `tool_request` simply waits, so the
  helper is unchanged. Deny answers the call as an error, "The person declined: …". Stop,
  Clear, closing the window and a dead helper all answer a pending confirmation as declined.
  An MCP caller is never asked: the rule belongs to the assistant's lane, not to the tool. Both
  lists are one table in one file, with a "withheld" or "ask first" column and a reason on
  every row; the helper never sees a withheld tool, and the lane refuses one if it is called
  anyway. Risk accepted: recording and cloud transcription stay menu-only, and every file
  written costs a click.
  **Amended 2026-10-01, by #40**: `close_project` is withheld, always: closing a project
  closes the window the conversation lives in (AI-5).
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-10**: `transcribe_for_fillers` is withheld, always, with R6-2's
  reason, pointing at Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, which shows what is uploaded and what it costs.
- **AI-8 — The key is the person's own, and is R6-5 and R6-12's key in everything but the
  vendor.** It lives in `SecretStore` under `anthropic-key`; the one override is
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, read only as R6-5 amended says. It is never a tool argument, a launch
  argument or an answer, and is handed to the helper on stdin only (§1, §3i). R6-9's
  `-RCSecretFolder` keeps proofs away from the person's file. R6-5's "integrated AI offering"
  is THIS, and it does not unblock C2 (#125), which still needs the caller's identity. Risk
  accepted: a `0600` file rather than the Keychain, for R6-5's measured reason.
- **AI-9 — History is append-only, and end-of-turn compaction is the one rewrite.** Rasterize's
  rule, for the same reasons: Opus 5.5 rejects replayed thinking after an edited prefix, and an
  unchanged prefix keeps the cache warm; compaction runs only at the end of a turn, past a
  threshold (§1). Risk accepted: old renders stay in context until compaction.
  **Amended 2026-10-01, by AI-20 (#151)**: compaction can be turned off or its threshold
  changed in Settings, and with "Clear old tool results" on, the API's clearing is a second
  rewrite — of what the model sees in a request past 150 000 tokens, possibly mid-turn, not of
  the helper's history. Each clearing breaks the prompt cache once.
- **AI-10 — Each tool call the assistant makes is its own undo step,** exactly as an MCP call
  is. A turn is not grouped, and the Edit menu names the step as it would for the same call
  from MCP (§6.4). Risk accepted: a ten-call turn is ten Undos.
- **AI-11 — The default model is `claude-opus-5-5` at medium effort.** The model is a person's
  setting, chosen in Settings' Assistant pane; like the key, no tool reads or writes it
  (§6.2). Risk accepted: the costliest default, paid with the person's key.
- **AI-12 — A tool call that arrives during a live gesture waits for mouse-up, then runs.** It
  applies to every caller, MCP and the assistant alike, because the lane (AI-2) is shared.
  "Live" means any open `ProjectDocument.isLiveEditing`: a timeline, canvas or inspector-slider
  gesture. A waiting call is never refused and never lost; before this, a call run between two
  ticks of a drag answered ok and was then undone by the next tick (#144; road map 12 §7 D2).
  The call lands above the gesture's own undo step. It is reversible: the wait is
  `AgentLane.onMainWhenIdle` alone. Risk accepted: a call, and the lane's lock with it, waits
  as long as the mouse is held down.
- **AI-13 — The assistant's one base-URL override is `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL`, and with it set
  no key file is opened.** The helper's `api_base` comes from this environment variable alone
  (the shared `protocol.ts` calls it "an environment variable of its own"; A0's F and T rows
  used it). Plain `http` is accepted only for a loopback host, as R6-9 allows for AssemblyAI;
  any other value refuses the session by name. This is AI-8's R6-9 made explicit:
  `-RCSecretFolder`, from the argument domain, names the folder of `anthropic-key`; with the
  override set and no `-RCSecretFolder`, NO `FileStore` is built and the store is an empty
  `MemoryStore`, so the person's file is never read; the store is read first and
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` second (R6-9 (d)). A variable rather than the argument domain because a
  variable cannot be persisted in the app's defaults, which is R6-9 (c)'s reason. Risk
  accepted: a person who exports it sends their environment's key, and only that, to the
  server it names.
- **AI-14 — A selection change that is not a click on a clip leaves the Assistant tab
  showing; a click on a clip still shows Clip.** The inspector's switch to Clip on a changed
  selection (`InspectorViewController.refresh(isLive:)`) runs only from the Media and Document
  tabs. The assistant's own calls change the selection mid-turn, and a tab that jumped to Clip
  under the person would hide the reply and the ask-first row they are waiting on.
  `clipPicked()` — a click on a clip in the timeline or canvas — still shows Clip from any
  tab. Risk accepted: a selection made by an MCP caller or a menu item while the Assistant tab
  shows does not bring the clip's properties forward; a click does.
- **AI-15 — The window's live context rides on each person message; the system prompt is fixed
  for a session.** `AssistantSession.send` writes the person's text behind a
  `<framejob_context>` block (`AssistantLiveContext.swift`): the project's name and path, the
  open nest, the playhead and the selection, as they are at send time. The system prompt, the
  tool-search guide and the compaction instructions are written once, in `configure`, and never
  change for the session. `configure` is the helper's only system channel and `agent/` is one
  diff with Rasterize (#147); a system prompt that changed per turn would break AI-9's
  unchanged prefix and the prompt cache; and the playhead and selection change between turns.
  Risk accepted: about sixty tokens on every message, and the block is the state at send time,
  so after its own edits the model re-reads with `get_project`.
  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): `<reelcut_context>` is now `<framejob_context>`.
- **AI-16 — Stop stops a running `export` or on-device `transcribe`; any other running call
  finishes.** Each call the session submits carries a per-call token through
  `AgentLane.submit`, and Stop cancels the running call's token. The lane answers a call whose
  token is already cancelled when it takes the lock "Cancelled by the user." without running it.
  A running `export` links its token to `Exporter.cancel()`, which only sets flags (G-17's
  cross-thread hazard does not arise; the writer removes its part-file), and an on-device
  `transcribe` links it to its `Transcriber.CancelToken`, the transcribe sheet's own path; the
  model gets the tool's own sentence ("The export was cancelled.", "The transcription was
  cancelled."). Before this, Stop only stopped the helper's turn, and an export in flight wrote
  its file to the end (#149). Risk accepted: `render_frame`, `render_graphic`, `import_media`
  (an opt-in ffmpeg conversion included), `save_project`/`new_project` and the main-thread tools
  run to their end; Clear, closing the window and a dead helper still let a running call finish,
  its result dropped, as before; cloud `transcribe` is withheld (AI-7) and not linked.
  **Amended by #326**: `export` answers at once, so Stop no longer reaches it; a queued export
  stops by `cancel_export` or the Export Queue's Cancel.
  **Amended 2026-10-23, by TR-11**: Stop also reaches `get_transcript`'s on-device run, linked to its `Transcriber.CancelToken` the same way, and the model gets "The transcription was cancelled."
- **AI-17 — The transcript is one selectable text, and the composer is multi-line with K-2's
  Return** (issue batch B18, #153, #154). The transcript is one non-editable text view: the
  entries in order, one "\n" between them, so a selection and a plain-text copy cross entries;
  a reply that is still extending edits only its own range. The layout dump reads the entries
  as parts the transcript names (id `assistant.entry.<kind>`, text, rect), since one text view
  has no subview per entry. The composer grows from one line to five, then scrolls. A bare
  Return or keypad Enter (⇪ allowed) sends while idle and beeps otherwise; it never answers a
  question. Return with ⇧, ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ inserts "\n", K-2's rule through the same
  `TextEditKey.route`; nothing is routed while an input method has marked text. Tab and ⇧Tab
  move focus, as the single-line field's did; they never type a tab into the message (amended
  by K-4: they, and a Return that sends, hand the keys back to the editor). The
  composer's typing undo is its OWN `UndoManager`: ⌘Z in the composer undoes typing, and typing

diagnosis and are never the budget. The budgets are the owner's numbers, committed; an agent
  never raises them.
- **P-4 — Spend shown in the app is Frame Job's own**, from its ledger, and says so. The Anthropic
  Console is the truth for the account.
- **P-5 — The spend ledger and the price cache are the person's, and a proof never touches them.**
  Both live in the spend folder, `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/` (`spend.jsonl`, one JSON
  line per priced response; `anthropic-prices.json`, the helper's daily copy of LiteLLM's table).
  `-RCSpendFolder <path>` replaces the folder, read from the argument domain alone (R6-9 (c)). With
  `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` set and no `-RCSpendFolder` there is NO spend folder: no ledger line is
  written, no cache is kept, and the helper prices from its bundled table and says so. The refresh
  fetches LiteLLM's raw `main` file; `-RCPriceFeed <url>` (argument domain) replaces it, and with
  the base URL set the cache is handed to the helper only together with `-RCPriceFeed`, so a proof
  never reaches LiteLLM. The helper refuses a feed that is neither https nor http to 127.0.0.1,
  localhost or ::1. A turn is priced with the prices in force at its `turn_started`; a refresh that
  settles mid-turn applies from the next turn. Risk accepted: two sessions opened at once may both
  fetch.
  **Amended by NM-4** (rename R0): the spend folder `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/` is now
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.
- **P-6 — The proofs' ledger is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job Proofs/spend.jsonl`, and
  every paid proof request is held to the month's budget in it before it is sent.** It is outside
  the repo, so it survives `rm -rf tools/proof/work` and a fresh clone and is shared by every
  worktree, and outside P-5's spend folder, which is the person's. `tools/proof/budget.py` is its
  only writer: one JSON line per event (`reserve`, `settle`, `refused`; `format` 1, `at` in UTC,
  `service`, `kind`, `id`), appended in one write to a file created 0600 in a folder created 0700,
  never a key, a header, a body or a text. The month is the UTC calendar month. A month's total for
  a service is a fold: a `reserve` made in the month counts its largest `settle`, or its `worst`
  while it has none; a `settle` with no `reserve` counts its own dollars in its own month; a
  `refused` counts nothing. The read, the fold and the append happen under one exclusive `flock` on
  the file, and a request is refused (`budget: …`) when the month's total plus its worst case would
  pass P-3's budget. It fails closed: a line that does not parse, or a ledger that cannot be read or
  written, refuses every paid request until a person repairs it. The worst case is the dearest the
  request can bill: for Anthropic, the relay's measure of the body and `max_tokens` at each token
  class's dearest rate over every row and `above_200k` tier of the price table; for AssemblyAI, the
  planned seconds at `AssemblyAIRates`' two rates added (speakers included). A reply is settled at
  the table's price; usage the table cannot price (an unknown model, a mode it has no rate for)
  settles at those dearest rates, and a reply whose usage cannot be read settles at its
  reservation. Only a keyed live run writes this ledger: rehearsals and verifications use scratch
  ledgers of their own. The budgets are constants in `budget.py`, pinned by `budget_proof.py`.
  Risk accepted: fast, priority and US-only usage is counted at the dearest standard rates (the
  helper requests none of them); a torn or hand-broken line stops every paid proof until a person
  repairs it. A keyed run of either road map 6 or 8 spike (`cloud_spike/`, `words_spike/`) reserves
  here too, through `cloud_live_ledger.spike_ledger`, beside its own $2.00 ledger (#163).
  **Amended by NM-4 and NM-7** (rename R0):
  `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut Proofs/spend.jsonl` is now
